newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - HSFO steady, LSWR down amid glut.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - HSFO steady, LSWR down amid glut.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil market was sluggish in thin talks on Tuesday despite slightly firmer SIMEX while LSWR edged down with ample May supplies, traders said.
As crude only inched up slightly and lacked direction, most fuel oil players adopted a wait-and-see attitude.

"The main market players are still staying on the sidelines, so the slow market may continue to be slow," said one trader, noting the absence of a local trader who has instead been active in the gas oil market in the past two months.
As fuel oil prices firmed in the Middle East, some traders said they expected fewer cargoes to come to Asia, tightening supplies to this region and supporting sentiment.
SIMEX futures on late Tuesday, traded 30 lots with June last traded 10 cents up to $98.00 and July bid/offered at $97.50/$98.20.
"Prices should be well supported although overall demand could remain slow," said one trader.
On Monday, two cargoes, one 180-cst grade and one 380-cst, were traded $98.50 and $91.00 per tonne respectively but traders said the demand was only routine.
Demand from China remained slack, traders said.
Fuel oil swaps were slightly firmer than Monday's levels, with May at $98.25/$99.00 and June at $97.25/$98.00.
In the LSWR market, traders said Indonesia's Pertamina had scheduled the 3.85 million barrels of LSWR for May allocation.
They also expected an additional 500,000 barrels to be rolled over from April, bringing the total to 4.35 million barrels in May.
"I think prices will only pick up in June when summer demand from Japan emerges," said one trader.
